24.0.0.en: Jeconiah: he is King Jehoiachin, who reigned three months over the kingdom of Judah and was then carried captive to Babylon.

24.0.1.en: Jeremiah saw a vision of two baskets of figs set before the temple of the Lord. He fixes the time of the vision: it was after Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon had carried away Jeconiah king of Judah, and had taken with him the great men of the Jews and the craftsmen skilled in the various trades from Jerusalem, and carried them all captive to Babylon.

24.0.2.en: The presence of the two baskets before the temple of God means that the Jews, of their different kinds, stood before God for Him to judge them, since everything is naked and open before His eyes. God allowed Jehoiachin to be carried captive to Babylon because of his evil. The king of Babylon carried away the best of the Jews to work in the capital of his kingdom, which made it flourish and grow strong, and among them were prophets and godly men. The fig fruit signifies unity, for it contains small seeds, none of which has any value in itself, but gathered together within a single skin they give it a sweet taste, just as the believers are gathered into one body, which is the Church, the Body of Christ.

24.1.0.en: Although the two baskets contain one fruit, the fig, there are two entirely different kinds inside them, and figs are of three kinds:

24.1.1.en: 1- The first-ripe fig: the firstfruit of the fig, which appears in the month of June. It is a very good fig, that is, the best kind of fig.

24.1.2.en: 2- The summer fig: a good fig which ripens and is gathered in the month of August.

24.1.3.en: 3- The winter fig: the fig which remains on the tree throughout the winter until the beginning of spring. It is a very bad fig which cannot be eaten.

24.1.4.en: Of the two baskets before the temple of the Lord, one had very good figs, that is, of the first kind, while the other had very bad figs, of the third kind.

24.2.0.en: God asked Jeremiah what he saw in the vision, and he answered that he saw very good figs in the first basket and very bad figs in the second. God asked this so that the prophet would declare his clear distinction between the two kinds. The two kinds are the righteous Jews and the wicked Jews. The first kind are those who obeyed God, went into captivity and kept His commandments; the second, bad kind are those who remained in Jerusalem and held fast to idol worship and all their evils.

24.2.1.en: God is the searcher of hearts and minds, and we are all exposed before Him. So do not persist in sin, for He sees you; and at the same time He greatly values your repentance, your striving and your attempt to draw near to Him. Remind yourself every day that you stand before Him to give an account of your stewardship, so that sin may not seduce you and you may not lose your crown.

24.3.0.en: God declares that the good figs are the Jews who were carried captive to Babylon. They lost their place beside the ruined temple, but they held fast to the commandments of God. So God blesses them with good because of their obedience to Him and their acceptance of discipline for their sins, since they listened to His prophets; God accepted their repentance and blessed them.

24.3.1.en: If affliction comes upon you, accept it as discipline from God for repentance and for the correction of your faults, and know that God is able to bless you within the affliction, so that you experience Him and behold Him more than at any time in your life.

24.4.0.en: God promises those who obeyed Him and came into captivity that He will bless them for accepting discipline, that He will reward them by returning them to Jerusalem and establishing them there, that He will build the temple for them and build them up in a strong spiritual life, for He is God, who is able to do all things.

24.5.0.en: God also promises His repentant children that He will give them a heart inclined to Him, that is, feelings of love directed toward Him. He also declares that He sets them apart as His people and cares for them because of their repentance.

24.6.0.en: God speaks of those who will disobey Him and cling to material things and evil, such as Zedekiah the king, the last king of Judah, and his close servants who govern the land, and the remaining people in Jerusalem and Judea who refused to go into captivity. They will be in a wretched state like the bad figs, because in their hypocrisy they thought that their remaining in Jerusalem was good and right, while their hearts were full of evil and idol worship.

24.7.0.en: Jeremiah prophesies about the wicked who remained in Jerusalem that God will abandon them and they will be in anxiety, because they relied on themselves and rejected God. In their weakness they will even become an example of contempt and mockery among the peoples, all because of their disobedience to God. They will also be driven out of Jerusalem and subjected to many troubles, for some of them went to Egypt and suffered many hardships there.

24.8.0.en: God decrees that He will punish them with three afflictions:

24.8.2.en: 2- Their extreme poverty and their hunger even for necessary food.

24.8.3.en: 3- Their being struck with severe diseases through pestilences that weaken them and destroy some of them. By these blows they will die and will not benefit from being in the Promised Land, because being in holy places without walking in holiness is of no benefit.

24.8.4.en: Benefit from every spiritual opportunity offered to you, so that you may know God through it and enjoy fellowship with Him, lest all these opportunities condemn you; for God sent them to you because He loves you.

25.0.0.en: Jeremiah fixes the time of the prophecy mentioned in this chapter as the fourth year of Jehoiakim king of Judah, which is at the same time the first year of Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon, namely 604 BC, after Nebuchadnezzar's victory over Necho king of Egypt at the battle of Carchemish in 605 BC, by which Babylon took possession of all Judea. He speaks of the Babylonian attack, coming swiftly to destroy Jerusalem and Judea, and warns his people for the last time so that they may repent.

25.1.0.en: This prophecy is addressed to those who dwell in Jerusalem and Judea, that is, the whole kingdom of Judah. Jeremiah dictated this prophecy to his scribe Baruch the prophet, who presented it to King Jehoiakim, and he burned it (Jer 36:1-26); Jeremiah wrote a second copy of it. This prophecy comes in order after the first twenty chapters of this book, and this book, or scroll, became the nucleus for the gathering of the rest of his prophecies (Jer 36:27-32).

25.2.0.en: Jeremiah declares that the beginning of his prophecies was in the thirteenth year of Josiah the king, the son of Amon, which is 627 BC. They continued for 19 years, then three months for the reign of Jehoahaz; after that Jehoiakim reigned for four years, and we reach the year 604 BC. That is, Jeremiah's prophecies have extended up to now for 23 years, during which he warned them to repent and spoke to them the word of God. He says "rising early" because Jeremiah began his prophecies at an early age.

25.2.1.en: Pay attention to God's messages, in which He calls you to repentance in different forms, so that you respond to His love. And in proportion to your care for prayer and for obeying Him before your own desires, you will hear His voice clearly.

25.3.0.en: There is no excuse for the disobedience of the Jewish people, because God did not send them one prophet only, Jeremiah, but many prophets went before him, such as Elijah, Elisha and Isaiah; yet they rejected the word of God spoken by their mouths.

25.4.0.en: The prophecies of the prophets are summed up in a call to repent of the evil, which appears in two things:

25.4.3.en: If they repented of their sins, they would enjoy the good things of the Promised Land which God promised to the fathers Abraham, Isaac and Jacob; indeed it was in His eternal plan and love to give it to them. This land is a symbol of the new earth, that is, the Kingdom of Heaven, which God prepared in His first plan from eternity for the believers, that they might dwell in it with Him forever.

25.4.4.en: Consider God's love for you from eternity and what He has prepared for you in the Kingdom, so that you may reject all your sins, however beloved or habitual they are or however much all those around you walk in them, and thank Him for His love, and live for Him so that you may enjoy Him now and forever.

25.5.0.en: He clearly warns against the idol worship which the Jews made with their own hands in the form of various images, and warns them that by this they defy Him and provoke Him to anger, that perhaps they may repent and return to Him; and if they insist on worshiping idols, He will be compelled to punish them.

25.6.0.en: Sadly, the people insisted on worshiping idols and provoked God to anger by their evil, so they deserved every punishment.

25.7.0.en: God shows one of His attributes, "the Lord of hosts," to declare His power, which is able to punish them for their evils.

25.8.0.en: The families of the north: the armies of the Babylonians.

25.8.2.en: An astonishment: they will be in terror.

25.8.3.en: An hissing: all people mock them for what has happened to them.

25.8.4.en: God declares His punishment for their disobedience: it is the use of the mighty Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon with his armies to attack the kingdom of Judah and shatter it, and to take possession of all the surrounding countries, laying them waste and killing those in them. Those who remain in them will be in terror and fear, and any who pass by them will mock and despise them for what happened to them because of their sins.

25.9.0.en: The millstones: the plural of the mill, the stones used anciently to grind grain. The punishment will include many things:

25.9.1.en: 1- The banning of joy and gladness, represented by the joy of new marriages and the use of musical instruments in merrymaking. This is a symbol of the absence of joy in God, and sorrow takes its place because of sin.

25.9.2.en: 2- Hunger: the mill will not be used to grind grain for the food of man and beast, since there will be no grain to grind, so they suffer hunger and die. This is a symbol of hunger for the word of God.

25.9.3.en: 3- The absence of light because of the destruction, which is a symbol of the darkness of sin.

25.10.0.en: Here he fixes the duration of the captivity of the kingdom of Judah, or the Babylonian captivity, when Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon occupied all the land of the Jews and the countries around it. He fixes this period at seventy years, beginning in 609 BC when Jeremiah announced this prophecy, to 536 BC when the first group of Jews returned to Jerusalem under Zerubbabel in the days of Cyrus king of the Medes and Persians. That is, the seventy years are approximately the duration of the Babylonian kingdom; then Babylon fell and the kingdom of the Medes and Persians arose, at the beginning of which the return of the Jews to Jerusalem from captivity began.

25.11.0.en: God used Babylon to discipline His people so that they would repent, although the Babylonians were wicked and worshiped idols. After the people of God repented, He brought them back from captivity, and punished the Babylonians for their evils and their wrongs against His people, so that great Babylon was destroyed by the hand of the Medes and Persians, who reigned in its place.

25.12.0.en: He affirms that He will fulfill the prophecies of Jeremiah recorded in his book concerning the people of God and the Babylonians.

25.13.0.en: He decrees that the kings who enslaved His people and wronged them, and everyone who walked in evil, He will repay for their sins: Babylon will be overturned, and after it the Medes and Persians, and then the Greeks, that is, the Ionians.

25.13.1.en: Do not become proud if God blesses you and you become stronger than those around you. Rather, thank Him and repent of your sins, because if God disciplined another for his evil, He will discipline you also if you do not repent. So live with God and hold fast to His commandments, and you will live in security.

25.14.0.en: God declares His wrath in order to discipline all the peoples of the earth for their evil, that they may repent, for God is the God of the whole world and desires the salvation of all, even though He chose a people for Himself, the Jews, to be an example to the rest of the peoples, so that all may return to Him and believe in Him. This is what was accomplished in Christianity, as mankind from all lands believed in Him.

25.14.1.en: The "cup" he calls a cup of wine that makes a person lose his balance, and he means divine discipline; when the wrath of God comes upon them they lose their strength. Christ before the Cross called the sufferings a cup, that is, He drank the cup for our sake and died to redeem us, bearing the wrath of God and the punishment of sin on His head to free us from it (Mt 26:39). The law of Moses decreed that a woman accused of unfaithfulness to her husband was given holy water by the priest in an earthen vessel, with some of the dust of the tabernacle of meeting put upon it, and she drank this water, which was called the water of the curse. If her belly swelled and her thigh fell away, she was judged unclean and became a curse among the people for her evil. So this cup proclaims the wrath of God against the unclean.

25.15.0.en: The effects of God's wrath on the nations are that they reel, that is, lose their balance, and go mad, that is, lose their minds, because of the many slain among them. This declares that God's wrath will be severe because of their many sins.

25.16.0.en: Jeremiah took the cup, that is, the word of God from the cup of wrath, and made all the peoples drink by announcing this prophecy before God, His servants and all the people, and the news of this prophecy passed to all the peoples.

25.17.0.en: He begins with Jerusalem and the kingdom of Judah because they are the people of God who knew much about Him. He disciplines them before others, because they have no excuse if they reject God and walk in evil and idol worship despite their knowledge of God.

25.18.0.en: After this comes the discipline upon Egypt and its princes, because it was the power on which the people of God tried to rely. Egypt was proud and did not submit to God but walked in idol worship, so the wrath of God came upon it after Jerusalem.

25.19.0.en: The mingled people: those of the Egyptians who joined the children of Israel and lived with them. Uz: a country lying east of Egypt and south of the kingdom of Judah, where Job dwelt (Job 1:1). Ashkelon, Gaza, Ekron and the remnant of Ashdod: the most important cities of Palestine, that is, the discipline will come upon the Philistines.

25.20.0.en: The wrath of God comes upon the countries neighboring the Jews that lie to their east, namely: Edom: they are the descendants of Esau, living in the mountains of Seir.

25.20.1.en: Moab: they are the descendants of Lot by his elder daughter.

25.20.2.en: The children of Ammon: they are the descendants of Lot by his younger daughter.

25.20.3.en: All these peoples were hostile to the people of the children of Israel on many occasions.

25.21.0.en: The wrath of God extends to the countries lying west of the land of the Jews, namely:

25.21.2.en: a- Tyre: it lies on the coast of the Mediterranean and is famous for commerce.

25.21.3.en: b- Sidon: it lies on the coast beside Tyre and is famous for fishing.

25.21.4.en: 2- The isles: those in the Mediterranean, such as Malta and Crete.

25.22.0.en: The wrath of God also extends to the Arab tribes dwelling south of the Jews, namely:

25.22.1.en: 1- Dedan: descendants of Abraham, famous for commerce (Gen 25:3).

25.22.2.en: 2- Tema: they dwell in the desert regions beyond Haran (Gen 25:15).

25.22.3.en: 3- Buz: descendants of Nahor, Abraham's brother (Gen 22:21); they dwell on the road between Damascus and Mecca.

25.22.4.en: 4- All that are in the utmost corners: those with the hair cut round; it was among the rites of worship of some gods to cut the hair in a circle, leaving a round area on top of the head, and these are Arab tribes.

25.22.5.en: The wrath of God includes all the kings of the Arabs and their tribes spread throughout the Arabian peninsula, and likewise "the mingled people," that is, those of the Arabs who attached themselves to the Jews and lived with them.

25.23.0.en: Zimri, Elam and the Medes: countries lying in the far east, upon which the wrath of God will also come.

25.24.1.en: The wrath also includes the countries north of the land of the Jews, whether near to them or far from the Jews; these countries will rise against one another, so the wrath of God will include all people because of their evil. In the end, the wrath of God comes upon Babylon, as the kingdom of the Medes and Persians lays it waste.

25.25.0.en: God declares His wrath against the peoples of the earth for their sins, so He says to them through Jeremiah: drink the cup of wine, that is, your evil lusts and idol worship, until you lose your balance like drunkards, and vomit, that is, come to a base and wretched state, and become empty after what is within you is brought out, that is, you become weak; then you will fall silent because of your shame and terror before the many slain among you.

25.26.0.en: And if they refuse to drink the cup, that is, refuse to hear the teachings and prophecies of Jeremiah, he assures them that the punishment is certain, that is, they will drink the cup of divine wrath.

25.27.0.en: The city which is called by my name: Jerusalem, because the temple of God is in it.

25.27.1.en: You: all the pagan peoples of the world.

25.27.2.en: God declares that His wrath will come upon His children who worship Him in His temple in Jerusalem because of their evils, and all the more will His wrath come upon all the peoples of the world because of their evil. Although He permits the wicked, such as Assyria and Babylon, to discipline His children, or the countries surrounding the Jews, such as Edom, Moab and the children of Ammon, to wrong them, all this is temporary; afterward He disciplines all who wronged His people, because they are wicked and pagan.

25.28.0.en: As they that tread the grapes: the shout of those treading grapes in the winepresses after they have been gathered is strong.

25.28.1.en: God likens Himself to a lion that lets out his fearful voice to all the animals; that is, God declares His wrath against all the peoples of the world and punishes them all, that they may believe in Him and return to Him. He also likens Himself to the shout of those who tread grapes in the winepresses.

25.29.0.en: God expresses the intensity of His wrath by the noise; that is, the loud voice and the great tumult heard everywhere in the world, because God stands as an adversary before the peoples of the world and judges and tries them, showing their deserving of punishment, and punishes them for their evil.

25.30.1.en: God declares that His wrath will fall on all the lands of the world because they are wicked, so the wrath comes upon one country after another to alert everyone to faith and repentance. By the great whirlwind he means the Babylonian attack, which sweeps over the whole earth and kills many.

25.30.2.en: Today you have an opportunity to repent before the day of judgment comes or severe afflictions befall you and you become preoccupied with them and it is hard for you to return to God. Offer your repentance today before God, and pledge to live for Him and remain steadfast in His Church.

25.31.1.en: Lamented: people mourn them with the well-known words of lamentation.

25.31.2.en: Gathered: their corpses lying in the streets are collected.

25.31.3.en: He describes the Babylonian attack that will cover the whole earth, that is, most of the countries known at that time, and kill many of them. Because of the multitude of the slain there is no opportunity to mourn the dead or even to lift up their bodies and bury them, because the living who remain flee from the face of the sword; so terror is in every heart, and the corpses become putrid, giving off foul odors everywhere, as human waste has a foul odor.

25.32.0.en: By the shepherds he means the leaders of the people, the teachers and those responsible for guiding and caring for the people of God. He warns them that their punishment has come, and they will be broken like a precious vessel and shattered. In another translation, instead of "a pleasant vessel" it says "the desirable rams," that is, they will be slaughtered like fattened rams. In sum, they will perish for their evils and their neglect of teaching the people the commandments of God. Therefore God calls them to weep and to humble themselves in the dust in repentance before Him before God strikes them by the hand of Babylon and scatters them far from their land.

25.33.0.en: A way to flee: a resolution and a rescue.

25.33.1.en: And if these shepherds try to flee from the Babylonian attack, they will find no opportunity, for it will overtake them and kill them, or seize them, humble them and enslave them.

25.34.0.en: These shepherds weep and cry out because they found no pasture for their flocks because of the Babylonian devastation that comes upon them; what is meant is that they will be in severe hunger and distress.

25.35.0.en: Peaceable folds: the green pastures in which the flocks graze quietly and securely. Terror and fear prevail because of the Babylonian attack, so everyone is disturbed and flees, and there is no opportunity for quiet work such as shepherding; consequently the sheep grow weak and die, and man is exposed to hunger.

25.36.1.en: He likens Babylon to a young lion that has come out of his den to prey on and shatter the nations of the world, and he describes it as oppressive because it plunders the spoils of all the lands and lays them waste.

25.36.2.en: Take care to shepherd those around you and draw them to Christ, show them love and warn them to guard against mistakes, so that you keep them and keep yourself from the wars of the devil.

25.36.3.en: Jeremiah's sermon in the temple and the attempt to kill him
